title: Non-quota append failures are terminal, never recovered, and re-reported for every incoming fragment
test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-094: a failed append is not reported again for every fragment, and the broken SourceBuffer gets nothing more', 'VAL-094: recovery takes a fresh init segment of the same generation and appends to the new SourceBuffer', 'VAL-094: failures beyond the recovery budget end in exactly one error', 'VAL-094: media appended after a recovery ends the failure episode and renews the budget', 'VAL-094: a MediaSource that closes under the player is recovered, and a closed one the player let go of is not', 'VAL-094: a video element error is recovered the same way, and stop() removes its listener' (and the guard 'VAL-094: a full SourceBuffer (QuotaExceededError) is still trimmed and retried, not treated as a failure', which passes before and after)
proof: On the unchanged player the six VAL-094 tests failed for the issue's reasons. With appendBuffer throwing InvalidStateError and 11 more fragments arriving, onError got 'SourceBuffer append failed' 11 times where none was expected (one per fragment, no recovery). 'the failure asks for a fresh init segment' expected 2 get-media-init requests, actual 1 (no recovery attempt). The budget test failed at 'failure 1 is recovered, not reported' (the first failure was already the terminal error) and the episode test at 'the answer builds a new MediaSource' (expected 2, actual 1: the answer for the same generation was ignored). The sourceclose and video error tests failed at 'the player listens for ...' (expected 1 listener, actual 0). After the fix all pass: a non-quota append exception, a SourceBuffer 'error', a MediaSource 'sourceclose' and a video 'error' all go to handleSourceBufferFailure, which lets the broken MediaSource go with its queue and generation (so nothing more is queued for it or appended to it, and a media-init of the same generation passes the duplicate check) and rebuilds through resetAndRequestInit. The rebuilds are counted until media goes into a rebuilt SourceBuffer (the init segment alone does not count) and capped at MAX_INIT_TIMEOUT_RETRIES (3); the fourth failure in a row is the single onError and the single 'error' state, with no further request, append or report. Two temporary mutants confirmed the tests bite: counting the init segment as success fails the budget test, and not ending the episode after a media append fails the episode test. lint and typecheck clean, npm test 853/853, vite build (into the scratchpad) exit 0.
